seo.title: Keep Singing for Palestine — Peace Concert | Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp
seo.description: Saturday 19 September 2026, Seoul. The Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp has changed its plan for the Banjul concert and is joining the street rally against the deployment of South Korean troops. Bookings are closed and will be refunded in full. Place and time to be announced.

intro.heading: We keep singing
intro.para_1: Rooted in the peace movement of Gangjeong Village on Jeju Island, now in its 19th year, Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp has gathered the will to oppose war and to resist through the language of music.
intro.para_2: This time we bring the songs of peace that rang out in Gangjeong Village to Seoul, to share them together.
intro.para_3: To stand with Korean civil society fighting against Israel's 78-year illegal occupation of Palestine and its genocide, we keep singing without pause!

rally.heading: From the rally to the concert
rally.body: At 14:00 we join the Emergency Action of Korean Civil Society in Solidarity with Palestine with a solidarity performance by Namsu, a versatile solo artist. Join us from the rally all the way to the concert!

lineup.heading: The people who sing
lineup.subheading: Four acts singing in Seoul for the liberation of Palestine

ihyeongju.name: Lee Hyeong-ju
ihyeongju.description: A singer-songwriter rooted in fingerstyle blues, weaving folk and jazz into his music. Since 2017 he has taken part in the New Minjung Music Compilation vols. 1–3 and sung at sites of social violence. Debut EP Atopy (2019), full-length album We Wanted to Keep Each Other (2023).

notice.heading: Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp is taking to the streets and the squares
notice.subheading: Against the US–Israeli war of aggression on Iran and the deployment of South Korean troops — on the change of plan for the Keep Singing for Palestine concert
notice.refund_body: Now that the 19 September concert at Banjul has become participation in a street rally, ticket bookings are closed. The organising committee will contact everyone who booked, one by one, and refund the full ticket price. There is no need to apply — please wait for us to reach you.
notice.para_1: In March this year, the United States and Israel invaded Iran. From the earliest days of the war, Trump demanded that South Korea send troops. The government, which at first said it was not considering a deployment, has recently shifted to saying it is "reviewing various options with the national interest as the top priority."
notice.para_2: There are forecasts that the presidential office will put a deployment consent motion before the National Assembly ahead of the Chuseok holiday and push it through within September. The leadership of the Democratic Party has ordered its members not to voice individual positions, the People Power Party actively supports the deployment, and conservative media are driving public opinion in favour of it.
notice.para_3: On Saturday 12 September, a large rally against the deployment was held in Seoul. Taking that as our starting point, we must now organise as many citizens as possible before Chuseok and show sustained momentum against the deployment. With the current government’s approval rating continuing to fall, the cry of the people gathered in the square is both an effective way to stop the deployment and the last line of defence.
notice.para_4: The organising committee of the Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp had planned to hold a peace concert in solidarity with the Palestinian liberation movement on Saturday 19 September at Banjul in Seoul. But the committee judged that this moment calls for more than solidarity through music — it calls for going out into the square and acting together with our fellow citizens. We are therefore changing the plan for the Keep Singing for Palestine concert and will join the anti-deployment rally in the square.
notice.para_5: Beyond taking part in the rally, we believe that raising and gathering many voices for peace and against war — before and after the rally, and in the various in-between spaces that open up around it — is what the Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp can and must do. As of now, it has not been announced whether the anti-deployment rally will be held on 19 September or on what schedule, and a rally for the liberation of Palestine and the Climate Justice March are also planned for the same day. Taking the fluid situation on the ground into account, we intend to combine performing in the street with joining the anti-deployment rally. We will share the details as soon as they are settled.
notice.para_6: The colonial rule and genocide inflicted on the Palestinian people and the war of aggression against Iran launched by the United States and Israel are by no means separate matters. They are tragedies of the same order and a chain of acts of aggression, in which imperialist militarism tramples the lives and peace of people and justifies violence. To sing for peace in Palestine is to oppose the war of aggression against Iran, and it is firmly tied to stopping the deployment of South Korean troops.
notice.para_7: Now, when we fear the deployment motion will be tabled before Chuseok, only the voices of the people gathered in the square can stop this dangerous war of aggression from running out of control. The Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp takes up the power of solidarity that music carries and goes out to the streets and the squares. Join us, so that songs for the liberation of Palestine may ring out as one with the cry against the war on Iran and against sending South Korean troops.
notice.block_musicians_body: We will stay in touch and confirm details as soon as the place and time of the street performance are set. The conditions may not be well suited to a performance, but we ask you to join us in a spirit of solidarity. The fees we agreed on will be paid as arranged.
notice.block_speakers_body: We will stay in touch and confirm details as soon as the place and time of the street performance are set. As far as you are able, we ask you to speak at the event and to join the rally against the deployment.
notice.block_guests_body: We are sorry that the concert you were expecting has changed. The organising committee will contact everyone who booked, one by one, and refund the full ticket price. We will also let you know the place and time of the street performance as soon as they are confirmed. As far as you are able, we ask you to join us at the street performance and at the rally against the deployment.
notice.block_host_body: You offered us your space in a spirit of solidarity, and we are truly sorry to cancel the booking at such short notice. We will not forget this, and we will look for and act on other ways to help your space keep going.
